title: Reduce two-coordinate A7+A1 COPY to a 44-vertex code (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written reduction with exact finite geometric certificates. For every positive block length d, fix any two A7 coordinates and allow every row independently to cancel either one. The exact minimum separate-term COPY cost in Matarener #5299's orthogonal-side-information model is

```text
C_d = 64d + beta_d(H44),
7d <= beta_d(H44) <= 8d,
71d <= C_d <= 72d.
```

Here beta_d is the minimum log2 message-range size of an index code on one explicit 44-vertex graph. Neither numerical endpoint is claimed sharp. This is a new reduction of the entire specified shift family, rather than a replay of the predecessor's two witnesses. No below-72 code, unrestricted-shift theorem, physical supplier, complete multiplication theorem or new kappa is claimed.

Six mutable terms and the fixed A1 term have new protected Petersen-plus-four witnesses, forcing 63d. Concatenating the remaining two messages codes a common 45-vertex graph, and a constructed row assignment attains that reduction. Removing one isolated vertex leaves H44 and the fixed charge 64d. Coordinate symmetry covers every pair.

Only `research/a7-two-coordinate-code-reduction/` is added. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Matarener [#5299](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5299) for the question, model and induced-demand reduction; adamgall [#2062](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2062) for the row normal form and frame binding; joaqcoo #1224, mightyOil #1248 and the retained decoder/width-pricing lineage. Blasiak, Kleinberg and Lubetzky's classical Petersen rate is a cited premise. Predecessor scientific executables and their witness counts were not replayed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19595294), [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19595359). The initial all-shift target is explicitly narrowed to this two-coordinate family. The selected #7000 frontier is unchanged.

## Evidence

Before, #5299 left arbitrary shifts with side information open after two complete witness certificates. After, a written coding argument and new protected cores give an exact reduction for arbitrary independent row choices in the specified family.

Local CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass. They check seven new protected witnesses, 1,440 local row-choice conditions, 196 transported witnesses across all 28 coordinate pairs, and all 946 unordered H44 vertex pairs against a separate combinatorial graph description. H44 has 462 edges. An independent seven-set and an actual rank-eight fitting encoder certify the remaining interval. Literal decoders check 22,012 outputs, and nine controls reject. These counts enumerate finite premises and decoder fixtures, not nonlinear codes or complete shift assignments.

Both registered commands pass locally, individually timed at 0.12 and 0.11 seconds. Metadata/source pins and committed-byte/source-history checks pass for all seven files at `6e759ce3eb6c30dbd04a6542af20f7b51ab7694b`. Receipts are generated from recomputed results and package hashes; none is handwritten. `git diff --check` passes.

From the repository root, run these exact commands. An equivalent CPython 3.12 path may replace the local installation.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/a7-two-coordinate-code-reduction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/a7-two-coordinate-code-reduction/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a7-two-coordinate-code-reduction
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/a7-two-coordinate-code-reduction --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_A7_TWO_COORDINATE_CODE_REDUCTION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The exact nonlinear graph rate is unresolved. The 71d lower bound is not asserted sharp. Three-coordinate or generic shifts, changed normals, punctures and joint COPY billing are outside the theorem. The universal block-length conclusion follows from the written proof rather than finite extrapolation.

Frame binding and the inherited message/side-information contract are cited mathematical premises. Gathering, native delivery, physical frames, dirty restoration, ownership, movement, stock, precision, compiler closure and the complete consumer remain unpriced. No selected assumption is discharged. Selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review and formal proof-kernel acceptance are unrun.

## Open next questions

- Determine beta_d(H44). A nonlinear lower bound of 8d would establish the 72d floor throughout this family; a shorter vector code would give a counterexample. Start with the explicit graph and checked fitting encoder. Binary minrank alone does not decide nonlinear vector codes.
- Derive the protected intersections and remaining message interface for three cancellation coordinates. The present two-part partition argument does not prove a bound for that larger family.

No follow-up is reserved. Work stopped at this first verified reduction.

## Related open work

- [#7169](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7169) constructs a non-coordinate masked completion on a fixed 93-line puncture. Its linear COPY71 is a different contract and quantity from this unpunctured nonlinear interval; no numerical agreement is inferred.
- [#7170](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7170) studies the coordinate scalar family on that 93-line puncture. It does not compute this A7+A1 side-information optimum.
- [#7168](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7168) studies Gram-class costs through 24 deletions. It does not price the nonlinear message contract here.
- [#7174](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7174) studies block realizability on a 96-line E8 complement. It does not compute beta_d(H44).

- [#7531](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7531) proves an all-field two-coordinate linear fitting rank for two pentagons sharing a hub. Its graph and linear query dimension differ from H44 and its nonlinear message-range rate; neither package computes a common numerical value.

No open PR found studies this two-coordinate A7+A1 family or H44. Merged #5299 is the main predecessor. Nick Petalas #5958 concerns two A8 simplex witnesses and is background only.

The completion check read this account's eight open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7527, #7528, #7530, #7531, #7532, #7533, #7534 and #7535. Apart from this PR, #7531 is the adjacent coding result described above. The others concern compiler suffixes, resolvent norms, permutation layouts, source counts, Schur residuals or tensor-splitting moments. None computes this A7+A1 or H44 quantity. No further computation audited those results.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `6e759ce3eb6c30dbd04a6542af20f7b51ab7694b`, [run 43467944399](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43467944399), [plan job 132031991016](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43467944399/job/132031991016), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the completed checks once and inspected that job's log. It reports exactly one failure among 760 tests, with 24 skipped:

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found in the CI verification document
```

The mismatch exists in unchanged canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. I inspected both files at that exact base. This PR changes neither file nor the failing test.

The package [replay job 132034443723](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43467944399/job/132034443723) was skipped after `plan` failed. Thus the mathematical execution evidence remains the local normal/optimized and registered checks at the published head. Hosted package replay remains unrun.

I also inspected the failed job logs and run metadata of rohanarun's [run 42905094314](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314) and dillona's [run 42903313790](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790). Both report the identical sole failing test and missing-command assertion, with 760 tests and 24 skipped. No repository-level repair, new commit, push, job rerun or retrigger was made. Maintainers retain the repair of main.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** package.

Seven new files in one isolated research directory. Shared implementations, predecessor evidence and the selected frontier are unchanged.
